message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/fmt && git show c9a57b9a -- include/fmt/format.h test/fuzzing/named_arg.cpp

message.content:
This is the fix! The commit `c9a57b9a "Fix incorrect assumptions about nul termination"` changes `named_arg_base::name` from `basic_string_view<Char>` to `const Char*`, and `init_named_args` from `{arg.name.data(), arg_count}` to `{arg.name, arg_count}`.

Wait, but this is confusing. Let me re-read. In the vulnerable version (HEAD `8a463068`), `named_arg_base::name` is `basic_string_view<Char>`. And `init_named_args` stores `{arg.name.data(), arg_count}`. So `named_args_[i].name` is a `const Char*` pointing to the argname buffer (not null-terminated).

In `get(name)`:
```cpp
if (named_args.data[i].name == name) ...
```
`named_args.data[i].name` is `const Char*`, compared with `basic_string_view<Char> name`. This constructs a `basic_string_view` from the `const Char*`, calling `strlen`. Since the argname buffer isn't null-terminated, `strlen` reads past the buffer.

The fix changes `named_arg_base::name` to `const Char*` and `init_named_args` to store `{arg.name, arg_count}` where `arg.name` is now `const Char*`. Wait, but that doesn't fix the strlen issue...

Actually wait, let me re-read. The fix changes `named_arg_base::name` from `basic_string_view<Char>` to `const Char*`. And `init_named_args` stores `{arg.name, arg_count}`. Now `arg.name` is `const Char*`. So `named_args_[i].name` is `const Char*`. In `get(name)`, `named_args.data[i].name == name` still constructs a `basic_string_view` from `const Char*`, calling `strlen`.

Hmm, that doesn't fix the strlen issue. Let me look at the format.h changes in this commit.
